claims.statement: The macOS MCP listener is off by default, Pro-gated, and binds only to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 with local-only network parameters; the mobile app does not start a local MCP listener.
Ordinary MCP requests require a constant-time-compared Bearer server token and, when supplied, a loopback-only Origin; ordinary request bodies are capped at 4 MiB.
The server token is generated from 32 secure random bytes, stored in this-device Keychain, and migration from a legacy iCloud value verifies the local copy before removing the cloud copy.
Rotating the server token stops transfers and MCP sessions, replaces the HTTP token, disconnects active HTTP connections, and requires clients to use updated configuration.

Initialized streamable MCP negotiates one of four supported versions, requires a session ID and matching version on subsequent requests except the March 2025 missing-header compatibility case, and retains transfer-active sessions past the normal 30-minute idle sweep; modern 2026-07-28 calls instead use operation handles without initialize.
Stopping, deleting, or expiring an MCP context cancels its copies, transfer capabilities, external authentication requests, and brokered secrets.

The external registry is an allowlist of Termind host tools plus request_user_secret and transfer tools; disabled tools are omitted from discovery and cannot be called, while disabling upload or download revokes that direction's coordinator.

External SSH authentication, host-key confirmation, and command-secret requests are queued through ExternalAuthCoordinator with client and session identity; MCP shutdown cancels external requests without cancelling Termind-origin authentication.
request_user_secret returns a one-shot secret handle rather than plaintext; ssh_exec consumes it only when its session run, host, tool, and purpose binding match.

Uploads and downloads use separate ten-minute, session-bound capability tokens in Authorization headers rather than the long-lived MCP token; they share a four-active-transfer budget and are revoked by session/host/stop/token-rotation/direction-disable events.
The upload capability is atomically claimed before its body is read, streams with backpressure, verifies exact length and SHA-256 before commit, and only resumes at a verified acknowledged offset.

A download ticket does no remote I/O until GET; downloads stream regular files without staging, support only a validated continuation Range, and do not mark success until source validation, send completion, checked close, and lease release succeed.

The termind-mcp bridge forwards newline-delimited stdin JSON-RPC to loopback HTTP with a Bearer token and stdout responses; for initialized clients it retains session and negotiated-version headers and deletes the session at EOF, while modern calls forward metadata-derived version, method, and name headers.

Client setup commands use direct HTTP for Claude Code, Copilot, and OpenClaw, while Codex and Hermes use the bundled termind-mcp bridge with URL and token environment variables; command generation is disabled when its required token or bridge is unavailable.

The MCP registry composes shared Termind tool definitions without a scratch workspace, AgentKit's user-interaction group, and four transfer tools; it selects acting mode before exported-name and disabled-tool filtering, so its 18 exports use acting ssh_exec and exclude terminal_suggest and scratch tools. Tests compare shared descriptors with the acting host subset.

The macOS AppModel supplies shared AgentHostServices resolver, connection pool, authentication registry, and background commands to its MCPServerController, which owns the external upload/download ticket coordinators and ties them to MCP sessions; iOS instead supplies AgentHostServices to MobileAssistantModel and constructs a separate ordinary SFTPTransferCoordinator, without constructing an inbound MCP listener or its transfer routes.

Both transfer-ticket tools use the MCP executor to validate a configured host and create a waiting capability without opening SSH, SFTP, local files, or the remote source; actual remote I/O begins only when the separate HTTP byte route claims the ticket.

Transfer status is authorized against the creating MCP run and a still-registered client, not possession of a ticket ID; ending the session removes that run's transfer tickets and makes their status unavailable.

The mobile MCP editor discovers outbound servers with MCPClient using manual Bearer or an OAuth authorization draft and browser interaction, retains per-tool access policies on rediscovery, and mobile settings require remoteMCP Pro access for adding or editing remote servers.

Desktop byte-transfer closures route SSH authentication and host-key interaction through the session-labeled external UI handler, then open SFTP via the injected authentication registry and pool; upload cleanup separately retries remote temporary-file removal after failed or cancelled attempts.

Download range syntax is validated before a ticket is claimed with malformed ranges returning 400; a valid open-ended range outside the remote file returns 416 after source inspection and restores the previous ticket state rather than consuming it.

The macOS AppModel keeps ordinary SFTP transfers separate from MCP ticket coordinators, revokes MCP host tickets on local or remote host removal, and stops MCP plus ordinary SFTP before closing shared agent background commands and connections on termination.

MobileAppModel handles host deletion by cancelling ordinary SFTP transfers and does not compose the desktop MCP server or its ticket routes; its assistant receives AgentHostServices independently of the mobile SFTPTransferCoordinator.

Desktop inbound MCP enablement, port and disabled-tool preferences remain device-local; the port setter clamps to 1024–65535, and changing the port while enabled restarts the listener, invalidating existing sessions and tickets.

The macOS settings UI resolves the bundled termind-mcp auxiliary executable, masks the token in command previews while copying the actual registration command, and disables only bridge-based registration when the bundled executable is absent.

Generated commands register the current localhost MCP URL; Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and OpenClaw pass a Bearer header over direct HTTP, whereas Codex and Hermes Agent register termind-mcp with TERMIND_MCP_URL and TERMIND_MCP_TOKEN; arguments are shell-quoted and regression-tested against shell injection.

The Assistant's embedded AgentKit MCPClient is an outbound, per-Assistant tool-catalog integration of configured remote servers and credentials with a conversation-scoped scratch workspace; the desktop MCP server instead builds its own restricted inbound registry, and iOS does not host its listener.

The MCP protocol limits initialized sessions and modern operation contexts together to 64; initialized tools require the initialized notification and matching session/version, while modern calls require matching version metadata and method/name headers and use an operation handle for related calls.

Extending the desktop MCP tool surface requires adding a tool to the explicit exported-name allowlist as well as the acting-mode registry and its dependencies; adding tools to the Assistant or a remote MCP server does not automatically export them inbound.
The stdio bridge only forwards JSON-RPC lines to the HTTP MCP route; upload and download file bytes require separate ticket-capability HTTP byte requests and do not pass through bridge stdin.

AssistantToolRegistry builds the Assistant catalog only for tool-call-capable models, admitting enabled remote MCP servers with nonconflicting namespaces and supplying each server's manual Bearer credential and OAuth-capable MCPClient; its conversation-keyed scratch workspace persists across runs without being shared across conversations.

The Assistant catalog registers AgentKit built-ins before Termind host definitions and discovered remote MCP definitions join afterward, preventing a Termind or remote tool name from shadowing a built-in.

Outbound remote MCP OAuth grants and client secrets are separated by server in a nonsynchronizing this-device Keychain service, rather than synced AI settings; the synchronized server configuration does not serialize grant tokens or client secrets.

The outbound MCP editor stages newly authorized OAuth grants in a draft that is discarded on cancel; committing saves credentials with configuration and rolls back credentials on configuration failure, while refresh rotations for previously saved grants persist before draft save.

Changing or deleting a configured outbound MCP server's authorization binding clears old device grants and cancels in-flight OAuth work; runtime token requests check the current binding before and after authorization, preventing retired configurations from initiating or completing another login.

Conversation-mediated outbound MCP OAuth browser requests transition a running conversation to waiting for user input and are cancelable on request cancellation or conversation stop; late callbacks do not create transcript or message content.
